issues.legal_issue: A company allotted land after its acquisition for industrial development by the development board is not a beneficiary or interested person entitled to participate in the landowners’ compensation reference.
material_facts: The land was acquired by the State for development by the industrial development board, and the acquisition notifications did not identify the later allottee as the beneficiary.
After the acquired land was transferred to the board, the board allotted it to the company under agreements that made the company liable for additional compensation payments to the landowners.
The landowners sought enhanced compensation in reference proceedings, and the company appealed the enhanced award, claiming it was an interested person who should have been heard.
issues.conclusion: The company, as a subsequent allottee, was neither a beneficiary nor a person interested entitled to participate in the compensation reference. The High Court erred in allowing its appeals and remanding the references; the Reference Court’s award was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under the scheme of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966, including Sections 28 and 32, land acquired for the development board vests in the State and is transferred to the board for development and disposal; a company allotted the land afterward is not thereby the beneficiary of the acquisition or a person interested under Section 2(11) of that Act or Section 3(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Liability under an allotment or lease agreement to pay additional compensation does not give the allottee a right to participate. The rules applicable to direct acquisitions for a company under Part VII and Section 50 of the Land Acquisition Act do not govern acquisitions under the industrial development statute. Peerappa Hanmantha Harijan v. State of Karnataka applied this distinction and distinguished Himalayan Tiles and Marble (P) Ltd. v. Francis Victor Countinho and U.P. Awas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Gyan Devi; the latter decisions therefore did not support participation in this case.

predicates.compensation_reference_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a reference to determine compensation for acquired land.
predicates.acquisition_for_development_board: The State acquired the land for development by an industrial development board.
predicates.land_allotted_after_acquisition: The board allotted the acquired land to a company after the acquisition.

issues.definition: When a compensation reference concerns land acquired for development by a board and allotted to a company only after acquisition, the company is not entitled to participate in the reference as an interested person.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court must follow a Supreme Court precedent that has considered and distinguished earlier decisions when that precedent governs the same issue.
material_facts: The High Court relied on earlier Supreme Court decisions concerning acquisitions under the Land Acquisition Act to hold that the subsequent allottee could participate in the compensation proceedings.
A later Supreme Court decision had considered and distinguished those earlier decisions and had ruled on the rights of a subsequent allottee in acquisitions under the industrial development statute.
The High Court did not follow that later decision, although it addressed the same statutory setting and issue.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was bound by the later Supreme Court decision; its failure to follow that precedent was contrary to Article 141 of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Article 141 makes the law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts in India. Where a later Supreme Court decision considers and distinguishes earlier authorities while deciding the same issue in the relevant statutory setting, the later decision governs. The Court relied on Peerappa Hanmantha Harijan v. State of Karnataka as the controlling decision and referred to Director of Settlements, A.P. v. M.R. Apparao, Rashmi Metaliks Ltd. v. Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority, and Bir Singh v. Mukesh Kumar on the binding force of Supreme Court precedent.

predicates.high_court_case: A High Court decides a case involving an issue of law.
predicates.controlling_later_supreme_court_preceden: A later Supreme Court decision governs the same issue in the relevant legal setting.
predicates.later_precedent_distinguished_earlier_ca: The later Supreme Court decision considered and distinguished earlier decisions on which a party or court relies.

issues.definition: When a High Court decides an issue governed by a later Supreme Court precedent that distinguished earlier cases, it must follow that later precedent.
